sources.entry: Veo - Google DeepMind's text-to-video model (currently Veo 3.1), generates cinematic video with synchronized audio and realistic physics. #paid

summary.name: Veo 3.1
summary.one_liner: Google DeepMind's video generation model that creates videos with natively generated audio, sound effects, and dialogue from text or image prompts.
use_cases: generating cinematic clips from text prompts
animating a still image into video
extending an existing clip into a longer video
creating videos with sound effects and dialogue
producing promotional or motion graphics videos
summary.what_it_does: Veo generates video from text prompts, images, or reference images, with audio (sound effects, ambient noise, and dialogue) generated natively alongside the video. Its listed controls include reference images for scenes, characters, objects, and style, scene extension using the last second of a clip, first and last frame transitions, camera movement controls, outpainting to change aspect ratio, and object insertion, removal, and motion-path control. Outputs are offered in 1080p and 4K. The page presents Veo 3.1 as the latest version and says it is accessible through Google Flow and developer platforms. Benchmark results are human preference studies reported by Google and are not independently verified.
notable: Native synchronized audio generation including dialogue and sound effects
Reference image, scene extension, first/last frame, and object insertion/removal controls
caveats: Listing tags the tool as paid (#paid), but the page itself does not state pricing
Page notes that natural spoken audio, especially short speech segments, remains an area of active development
Page does not specify access tiers or costs
